abstract: A numerical compilation forecast may be supported by a theorem, agreement on tested instances, or a structural model that happens to cover those instances. These warrants are not interchangeable. We separate them for an exact shared-tag Pauli block-encoding model and then test whether the resulting regime description transfers to another compiler family. An interpretable three-family formula first matches a prospectively staged panel, yet a frozen fresh instance refutes it: the formula returns 11 while the exact optimum is 10. A support-two normalization theorem yields a stronger forecaster that equals the unrestricted optimum for every admitted size under the unit structural objective; all finite implementation comparisons agree. Explanation remains separately falsifiable: a repaired borrow vocabulary fails on 64 hostile cases, and six of seven of its complete-census fibres contain mixed exact costs. A later per-block-permutation argument closes the previously open commuting-support-two sector, while one alternative global proof link remains explicitly open, and a second route is refuted by an exact counterexample. In weighted Clifford state preparation, a four-feature separator is minimal on the complete small-size domain, but the frozen next-size rule makes 32 errors on 120 states and shows no improvement under the specified shuffle null (p = 0.51). Exact cost, explanation, finite verification and transfer therefore require distinct certificates. The results concern frozen algebraic objectives and do not establish runtime, production-compiler, hardware or quantum-advantage claims.
title: Certified Cost Forecasts and Refutable Regime Maps for Exact Quantum Compilation
